name: Two Digit Strings
description: You are given two strings $$$a$$$ and $$$b$$$, consisting only of digits. In one operation, you can choose two adjacent characters in either of these two strings and replace them with their sum modulo $$$10$$$. For example, from the string $$$57246$$$ you can obtain the following strings in one operation: $$$\mathbf{57}246 \rightarrow 2246$$$; $$$5\mathbf{72}46 \rightarrow 5946$$$; $$$57\mathbf{24}6 \rightarrow 5766$$$; $$$572\mathbf{46} \rightarrow 5720$$$; Note that after such an operation, the length of the string always decreases by exactly $$$1$$$. You can perform any number of such operations (even zero). You have to make these strings equal ($$$|a| = |b|$$$ and $$$a_i = b_i$$$ for all $$$i$$$ from $$$1$$$ to $$$|a|$$$). Calculate the maximum possible length of the resulting equal strings.
input_specification: The first line contains a single integer $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \le t \le 2 \cdot 10^3$$$) — the number of test cases. The first line of each test case contains a string $$$a$$$ ($$$1 \le |a| \le 5 \cdot 10^3$$$), consisting only of digits. The second line of each test case contains a string $$$b$$$ ($$$1 \le |b| \le 5 \cdot 10^3$$$), consisting only of digits. Additional constraint on the input: $$$\sum (|a| + |b|) $$$ across all test cases does not exceed $$$10^4$$$.
output_specification: For each test case, print one integer — the maximum possible length of the resulting equal strings. If you can't make the strings equal, print -1 .
approach_summary: Express count as f(R) - f(L-1). Define memoized state dp[pos][tight][leading_zeros][cond] scanning digits from most to least significant in O(digits × base × states).

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 2242D — Two Digit Strings [439. Digit DP]
topic_editorial.summary: Digit DP counting values in range $[L, R]$.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: Counting valid integers in range $[L, R]$ can be decomposed into $f(R) - f(L-1)$, where $f(X)$ counts valid integers in $[0, X]$. Numbers $\le X$ can be formed digit-by-digit from the most significant position. The constraint that the prefix does not exceed $X$ is tracked by a single boolean flag `tight`.
